intro: Months show direction. Days show noise. Monthly success is where you honour progress, adjust goals, and choose the next theme.
buddyTip: Archive wins in writing — “logged 24/30 days,” “protein at lunch stuck.” Memory under-credits you.
mission: Open Progress for the last 30 days and write one keep / one change / one celebrate.
why: Without a monthly zoom-out, people either panic at plateaus or ignore real drift. A month is long enough to see body changes, habit strength, and whether your goals still match life.
Body change is more than scale weight: energy, training performance, clothes fit, hunger patterns, sleep. Monthly review holds space for those signals so the number alone does not bully the story.
Goals expire. Travel seasons, new jobs, injuries, and family rhythms need updated targets. Adjusting is maturity — not quitting.

what.lead: A complete monthly pass covers five areas.
points: Progress review — adherence, weight trend, protein/fibre themes
Body changes — scale, photos if you use them, how training feels
Habits — which rituals stuck (logging, water, walks) and which didn’t
Adjust goals — energy, protein, training load, or focus theme
Celebrate — name the hard thing you did consistently

misconceptions.myth: No scale change means the month was a failure.
misconceptions.truth: Recomposition, better adherence, and skill-building count. Check multiple signals before declaring failure.

misconceptions.myth: I should overhaul everything for a “fresh start.”
misconceptions.truth: Keep what worked. Change one lever. Fresh-start theatre usually deletes hard-won habits.

how.lead: Block 30–40 minutes once a month — same calendar ritual as bills or planning.
steps: Review Progress trends and rough Foodiary completeness
Note body and energy changes in plain language
List habits that ran on autopilot vs habits that needed force
Update one goal for next month; park the rest
Celebrate explicitly — message a Space friend or write it in notes
Set a single monthly theme: “protein consistency,” “earlier dinners,” “walk after lunch”
how.buddyHelps: Progress is built for zoom-out. Spaces let celebration become shared. Buddy coaching stays useful when goals reflect your current month, not last year’s fantasy.

sections.title: When to adjust energy goals
paras: If weight trend and honest logs disagree with your target for several weeks, adjust calmly. Large swings confuse both you and Buddy’s learning.
If life got harder (travel, stress, injury), temporarily prioritise adherence and protein over aggressive deficit.

sections.title: Celebration is maintenance
paras: Celebration reinforces identity: “I’m someone who logs and learns.” Skipping celebration makes the next hard week feel pointless.
Keep celebrations compatible with your goals — belonging and rest count more than compensatory restriction.

mistakes.quote: I’ll judge the whole month by the last three days.
mistakes.why: End-of-month noise (holidays, illness) is not the month. Look at the full trend.

mistakes.quote: Habits didn’t stick, so I’m not a “health person.”
mistakes.why: Unstuck habits usually need smaller design, not a new identity. Shrink the ritual and retry.

mistakes.quote: I hit my goal early, so I can abandon structure.
mistakes.why: Structure is how you keep results. Lighten intensity if you want — keep the logging loop.

encouragement: You are allowed to be proud of imperfect months. Direction plus honesty is already Scale Health Success starting with you.
